Pas de Fierté sans la Palestine : la sol: No Pride Without Palestine: Queer Solidarity Put to the Test
Des groupes 2ESLGBTQIA+ et QTBIPOC rompe: 2SLGBTQIA+ and QTBIPOC groups are breaking with Fierté Montréal, denouncing pinkwashing and organizing an inclusive, radical Fierté Indomptable.
Fierté Montréal répond-elle toujours aux: Does Fierté Montréal still meet the expectations of its community? Image credit: Sonia Ekyior-Katimi
Il y a quelques semaines sur les réseaux: A few weeks ago on social media, I saw several posts and stories announcing that QTBIPOC (Queer, Trans, Black, Indigenous and People of colour) organizations were cutting ties with the institution that is Fierté Montréal. It caught my attention right away.
Je savais déjà que <em>Fierté</em> faisa: I already knew that Fierté had been the target of several criticisms, notably over its ties to the police, its associations with companies complicit in Israel’s occupation of Palestine, and the way artists and individuals at the intersection of several identities (race, gender, queerness, etc.) were being treated.
J’avais vu plusieurs articles mentionnan: I had seen several articles mentioning the stances taken by some of these organizations, but rarely the reasons behind them. At least, not in depth, and without getting to the heart of the problem.
J’ai donc voulu parler à quelques-uns de: So I wanted to talk to a few of these organizations and understand what they were going through. Why decide to distance themselves from Fierté Montréal? Why are so many organizations speaking out on this? And above all, what do these organizations hope for the future?
<strong>Depuis le 7 octobre 2023 et l’ag: Since October 7, 2023, and the worsening of the genocide in Palestine, one question keeps coming up in Montréal’s 2SLGBTQ+ and QTBIPOC circles… Does Fierté Montréal still meet the expectations of its community? Several groups have distanced themselves from the organization, pointing to how far it has drifted from its radical roots, from an activist memory born in the streets, rooted in riots and built on the resistance and the voices of the most marginalized queer people. In the eyes of these organizations and collectives, Fierté now seems to be turning its back on all that. We spoke with them to understand what has happened in recent months, ahead of Fierté Montréal’s controversial parade this Sunday.
<em>Helem Montréal</em>, un organisme 2E: Helem Montréal, a 2SLGBTQ+ organization from SWANA (Southwest Asian and North African) communities, was the first to announce its break with Fierté Montréal. According to Yara Coussa and Samya Lemrini, two of its members, Fierté cannot claim to stand at the intersection of marginalized identities without supporting the Palestinian cause. For them, defending the fundamental rights of 2SLGBTQ+ people also means fighting, in the same movement, apartheid, colonialism and all forms of systemic oppression, here as elsewhere.
De fait, <em>Fierté Montréal</em> a offi: Indeed, Fierté Montréal only officially took a position on the ongoing genocide in Gaza on July 30, 2025, nearly two years after the events of October 7, 2023.
Selon <em>Helem Montréal</em>, c’est cet: According to Helem Montréal, it is this belated position that pushed the organization to publicly dissociate itself from the festival and to call on other queer groups to do the same.
« On a tellement voulu travailler avec e: “We wanted so badly to work with them [on this] and meet them halfway. Because we love our Pride! I’m not being hard on Fierté Montréal, honestly, my heart is broken,” says Samya, pointing to limits that, for her, are non-negotiable.
Leur rupture avec le festival prend raci: Their break with the festival dates back to May 2024. Like several other collectives, Helem Montréal was invited to a Fierté Montréal membership event. Its members saw it as a chance to open a space for dialogue on Palestine. At that gathering, the group therefore tried to bring in this perspective of intertwined Palestinian and queer struggles, an essential stance in the face of a genocide, Samya believes.
Samya leur a notamment envoyé la <l1>déc: Samya sent them, among other things, the International Court of Justice’s declaration underscoring the plausibility of a genocide being committed in Gaza, in the hope that Fierté Montréal would take a firm position.
Pourtant, ailleurs dans le pays, les cho: Yet elsewhere in the country, things are moving: <l1>St. John’s Pride, Fredericton Pride</l1> and <l2>Halifax Pride</l2> quickly cut ties with their Israel-linked sponsors and took a stand in favour of Palestine. In their statements, they say that refusing to show solidarity with Palestine, under the pretext of focusing on 2SLGBTQ+ rights, betrays the promise of intersectionality and liberation at the core of their commitment.
Cette tension s’accentue lors du défilé: The tension grew during the 2024 Pride parade, when Helem Montréal found itself marching near Ga’ava, an organization for Montréal’s Jewish LGBTQ+ community, which was waving Israeli flags, Yara and Samya say. On social media, Ga’ava regularly shares posts highlighting the involvement of queer people in the Israeli armed forces, which groups like Independent Jewish Voices Montréal call pure pinkwashing*.
Pendant le défilé de la fierté de 2024,: During the 2024 Pride parade, a peaceful march organized by Helem Montréal, Mubaadarat and Independent Jewish Voices took place to draw attention to the situation in Palestine. The demonstrators were surrounded by dozens of police officers, which reinforced the feeling of not being truly welcome at the march, Helem Montréal insists.
<em>Helem Montréal</em> indique être res: Helem Montréal says it stayed in touch with Fierté Montréal for several months to continue discussions about Palestine, the police presence during their march, and the festival sponsors’ financial ties to Israel.
Mais d’après <em>Helem Montréal</em>, ce: But according to Helem Montréal, these overtures were often left unanswered. On December 10, 2024, the organization cut its ties with Fierté Montréal, and announced it a month later, on January 22, 2025, on its social media.
<em>La Converse</em> a contacté <em>Fier: La Converse contacted Fierté Montréal about this lack of communication with Helem Montréal regarding its position on Gaza, but the organization did not respond.
La fin de cette collaboration entraîne u: The end of this collaboration set off a wave of support: other associations spoke up in turn and shared their own experiences with Fierté. At the heart of their accounts is the Palestinian cause, echoing those of Sudan, Congo, Myanmar, Tigray and Haiti, struggles tied to racism, misogyny and gender-based violence, the two Helem members explain proudly.
« Tout ce que je vois, les dénonciations: “Everything I see, the denunciations that are coming out, it’s all in light of the colonialism inherent in Fierté. All the struggles are interconnected,” says Samya, moved by the support received from queer and non-queer groups alike, such as Independent Jewish Voices Montréal, AlterHéros, Coalition Jeunesse LGBTQ, and CALACS of the West Island. “I took it as a hug,” she adds.
<strong><em>Fierté indomptable</em>, inv: Fierté Indomptable, created by and for the community
En réaction, une nouvelle initiative pre: In response, a new initiative has come to life: Fierté Indomptable. For the QTBIPOC and 2SLGBTQ+ groups involved, marching remains an essential act. They plan to keep marching, but in a spirit of autonomy and reclamation.
Créée par des membres communautaires iss: Created by community members from a range of backgrounds, the initiative was born of a “need and a necessity,” Yara explains. “A lot of LGBTQ+ people no longer felt safe at Fierté, no longer felt represented, so it came out of a desire for a Fierté that looks like us.”
Samya, elle, évoque l’héritage radical d: Samya speaks of the radical legacy of these struggles, which must be respected and honoured: “Pride was a riot, a rite for people who look like us, people who truly need representation, but not empty representation with no concrete action.”
<em>Fierté Indomptable</em> se présente: Fierté Indomptable presents itself as a resource for 2SLGBTQ+ people looking for community and collective support. A space built for everyone: parents, children, immunocompromised people, youth. A mobilization carried by the community itself, separate from banks, corporations and the police.
Pour ce faire, les propositions d’activi: To that end, the proposed activities are varied: activism workshops, visual arts, and even activities to keep children occupied. The programming was carefully designed to welcome any participant and to foster community mutual aid as well as diversity.
« Pour moi, ma communauté elle est diver: “For me, my community is diverse, it’s accessible, it’s neurodivergent, it’s autistic, it’s lesbian, it’s trans, it’s Arab, it’s Black, it’s Indigenous,” Yara explains.
Malgré les départs marquants de plusieur: Despite the high-profile departures of several organizations, some groups involved in the community scene have decided to stay affiliated with Fierté Montréal. They call for nuance and stress the delicate balances of collaborative work within a community.
Rafaël Provost, directeur général d’<em>: Rafaël Provost, executive director of Ensemble pour le respect de la diversité, an association that promotes living together and fights discrimination and champions an intersectional approach, welcomes us at the foundation’s offices in Sainte-Marie. When we discuss the situation, the organizer urges us to approach the issues without bias, with balance.
“It’s hard to navigate. It reflects everything else. There’s polarization, there’s division. We’re no longer talking to each other, and I think dialogue is really one of the keys to reconciliation. But it takes time, a lot of sensitivity, and it takes work from both sides,” he begins.
Engagé dans une démarche de rassemblemen: Committed to bringing people together, he nonetheless commends the organizations that are voicing criticism, which he considers an act of courage. “It’s important for organizations to remain consistent with their values and their actions,” he insists. Principles like respect and diversity must be reflected concretely. It’s not about judging who is good or bad, but about applying one’s values fairly, he says.
Concernant certaines collaborations crit: Regarding some of the criticized collaborations, such as with the Service de Police de la Ville de Montréal, he calls for caution and argues for a measured approach. For him, well-intentioned efforts must be distinguished from structural problems. He believes in gradual change rather than radical challenges.
À maintes reprises, ses mots font écho à: Time and again, his words echo a time when Fierté was experienced mainly as a space for coming together. “I think we also have the right to celebrate, but never without forgetting all the work that has been done, and what remains to be done. I find that marching makes a lot more sense. It’s simple and it’s powerful. It’s just humans walking. That’s what we need to do,” he says passionately, recalling a past Pride that left its mark on him and that he misses.
Malgré son insistance sur la complexité: Despite his insistence on the complexity of the dynamics at play, his attention turns to the commitments and future possibilities of the association he leads.
‍<em>Ensemble</em> restera membre de <em: ‍Ensemble will remain a member of Fierté Montréal, he confides. Although listed as a partner, the organization is not an active member behind the scenes at Fierté Montréal, he adds. His role, as he describes it, is more one of observation: he follows developments closely while staying focused on the mission and values of his own organization.
<strong><em>Fierté Montréal</em> prend l: Fierté Montréal speaks out, too late for some
Contactée par <em>La Converse</em> au su: When contacted by La Converse about the situation, Fierté Montréal initially responded to our request by saying it “will not comment further on the situation at this stage.” A follow-up requesting an interview was sent, but received no reply.
Toutefois, le 30 juillet 2025, <em>Fiert: However, on July 30, 2025, Fierté Montréal released a statement on its social media and by email, addressing “its position” on the Israeli-Palestinian conflict.
Le festival indique qu’il condamne le gé: The festival says it condemns the ongoing genocide in Gaza, expresses its solidarity with the Palestinian people, and wishes for the lives of 2SLGBTQIA+ people in Palestine, as everywhere in the world, to be respected and preserved.
<em>Fierté Montréal</em> note aussi sa d: Fierté Montréal also notes its decision to “refuse the participation of organizations that promote hateful rhetoric in order to prioritize the emotional and physical safety of communities,” stressing a refusal to instrumentalize its spaces in the context of the conflict.
Une semaine plus tard, le 5 août, l’orga: A week later, on August 5, the organization announced in another statement that “all communities are invited to take part in the festivities, following contact with representatives of the Jewish community to clarify the situation and ensure an inclusive and safe space for everyone, including 2SLGBTQIA+ Jewish people who wish to take part in the parade.”
Le Centre consultatif des relations juiv: The Centre for Israel and Jewish Affairs (CIJA) and its partner, the Jewish 2SLGBTQIA+ group Ga’ava, <l1>were re-invited.</l1>
En réponse aux dénonciations rendues pub: In response to the denunciations that had been made public and widely shared, Fierté Montréal also spoke out in February 2025, through a letter addressing the concerns expressed by several queer community groups.
Simon Gamache, le directeur général de <: Simon Gamache, executive director of Fierté Montréal and the signatory of the statement, wants to encourage a more nuanced understanding of how Fierté works, saying he is committed to representing diversity and bringing it together.
Malgré les points adressés par Gamache e: Despite the points addressed by Gamache and the Fierté team in their statement, no attempt at dialogue has been made yet, Yara and Samya say. Helem Montréal is nonetheless, they point out, the origin of the criticisms directed at Fierté Montréal. “The fact that they’re not doing it, to me, that shows me everything I need to know,” says Yara, visibly exhausted. The few efforts at dialogue came only after the organizations concerned spoke out publicly to criticize Fierté Montréal on social media.
